learner_operation: Determine the value class after at most one elementary simplification and select every containing set in N subset Z subset Q subset R subset C, excluding zero from N.

fixed_features.feature: The five basic sets and their nesting
fixed_features.justification: Tutorial Introduction 2d61ed1f-938f-51f3-8f72-19f2a9db35ea and canonical example establish these objects as the classification targets. Scripted sets are the next KP.
Every offered real or nonreal number belongs to C by the lesson definition; this constraint is mathematical.
All source instances ask membership for one number at easy difficulty.

answer_roles.role: Smallest containing set and resulting selection count
answer_roles.eligible_variation: N / Z / Q / R / C depending on value; all five are source- or lesson-supported.
answer_roles.observed: All five in fresh sample and 77 survivors; batch survivors contain N,R,C. See per-stage exact counts.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Fraction and decimal may be integer or noninteger; positive root may be integer or irrational, with zero at the boundary.
answer_roles.observed: Each fraction and decimal subgroup realizes three membership masks; radical four; conditional shortcut probes retained. Negative nonsquare roots are improperly excluded (separate restriction finding).

answer_roles.observed: Fresh generation uses only checkboxes; six-item archival replay contains only legacy positive-root radio. Two supplied source radio banks omitted (separate fidelity finding). No claim of radio-family decision coverage.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select exactly R and C for either sign of pi.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: A 0.2 uniform full-mask baseline is beaten perfectly, but knowing pi is irrational and hence real/complex is explicitly the source operation (3c87cce5-2762-52a9-b3ea-307f7f887046), not incidental formatting. Both signs retain this mathematical property.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Always check C (partial action, not a complete answer).
shortcut_probes.conclusion: The comparison baseline is a random boolean on the C field. All values are complex by the source hierarchy, so fixed C membership is necessary; it does not determine the other four fields.
